title: Verdict
description: A prediction produced by a seer. Stored as the YAML frontmatter of a Markdown file whose body holds the seer's reasoning.

id.description: Stable identifier, also the filename stem. Never reused, never renamed.

seer.description: The subagent that produced this verdict.

asset_class.description: Checked against the registered modules rather than listed here. A closed list would mean adding an asset class requires a schema edit, which contradicts the registry's whole point — see src/modules/asset-class.ts.

question.description: The question in full, as a sentence. Long enough that it cannot be a fragment like 'gold up?'.

probability.description: Exclusive bounds. A verdict at 0 or 1 is a claim of certainty, which is not a prediction — and under Brier scoring it is the one place a seer can lose everything on a single call.

due_at.description: When the question is about. Distinct from resolution.check_after, which is when the answer can first be read.

calibration_probe_of.description: Set when this verdict exists to calibrate a longer-horizon one. The relation and the minimum probe count are enforced separately.

resolution.description: Filled in at prediction time. Without it the verdict is unmeasurable and is not stored.

source.description: Fixed now, so that nobody can pick the flattering source once the result is out.

series.description: Series code, or the id of a frozen listing basket.

reference_period.description: The period being measured: YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-Www.

check_after.description: The first date the value can exist, read from the publication calendar rather than the calendar month.

rule.description: One comparison, no room for interpretation. The single-comparison shape is enforced by the resolution validator, not by this schema.

print.description: The first published value, never the revised one. Series get revised retroactively; scoring against a revision rewrites history.
